block: SW Line Items, leaf rows in cost centres APPLHFIN, APPLHHR, APPLHLSA, APPLHALT, APPLGENERAL, APPLBRNDCOMS, APPLMTOTAL, APPLRCALSTORES, APPLFIREFINING, CTRMSIG, INTEMERSIG, CRPOSSIG, TDDEINTSIG, CUSTLOYSIG, HEMERALD, PCTECHKCM, PCTECHMYHR
basis_scope: The 2026 Budget tab of the same file covers 35 technology cost centres and its scope on the line item tabs is cost centre APPLH_INFOTECH. Every one of the seventeen cost centres in this block sits outside that scope, so this block cites the tab nowhere. Every destination here rests on column facts in the line item tabs, on the portfolio and platform table in the structure document, and on rule citations into the other three block files.

rules.match: Column C equals CTRMSIG.
rules.evidence: Cost centre CTRMSIG carries column D value 'CTRM SIG ITEM'. The structure places the CTRM project platform under Commercial Fuels and states that sig item programs land on real project platforms. Every line in the centre carries the program in column N, including the monthly 'CTRM SIG ITEM' journals, the recharged thinkcell licence lines and the transfers of CTRM cost to the Singapore and United States entities.

rules.match: Column C equals CRPOSSIG, or column C equals APPLMTOTAL and column N reads 'RECLASS MAY TRF TO CRPOSSIG' or 'RECLASS JUNE TRF TO CRPOSSIG'.
rules.evidence: Cost centre CRPOSSIG carries column D value 'CONV RETAIL POS SIG ITEM'. The structure places the AmPOS project platform under Ampol Retail and names AmPOS as the point of sale program. The marketing operating centre routes on column N text, and column N naming the point of sale programme routes to AmPOS, which is the same route the sig centre takes. Documents 5119976154 and 5120459154 each carry both legs: the positive in CRPOSSIG, sheet rows 18712 at 46,078.47 and 18713 at 14,397.96, and the negative in APPLMTOTAL, sheet rows 12992 at minus 46,078.47 and 13105 at minus 14,397.96. The four lines net to zero inside the rule and both sides of each transfer stay visible. The Snowflake reclassification on document 5118145663 names its product in column N and stays on rule 16.

rules.match: Column C equals INTEMERSIG, TDDEINTSIG or HEMERALD.
rules.evidence: The three centres carry column D values 'EMERALD INTEGRATION', 'TDD EMERALD INTEGRATION' and 'PROJECT EMERALD'. The old model dashboard names the program 'Emerald-EGI' in its recharge by initiative table, and the structure places the EGI project platform under EG Integration and states that sig item programs land on real project platforms.

rules.match: Column C equals CUSTLOYSIG.
rules.evidence: Cost centre CUSTLOYSIG carries column D value 'CUST STRAT & LOYALTY SIG'. The structure places Ampol Loyalty & Martech under Ampol Customer. The centre nets to zero: the subscription and onboarding lines are offset by the half year reporting sig transfer, whose opposite leg sits in the brand centre and is held open at open item O21.

rules.match: Column C equals PCTECHKCM or PCTECHMYHR.
rules.evidence: The two centres carry column D values 'P&C TECH - KNOWLEDGE & CASE MANAGEMENT' and 'P&C TECH - MYHR'. The structure carries P&C as both portfolio and platform. Two documents corroborate from inside the line item tabs: document 5118043472 charges the ServiceNow HR Service Delivery professional fees of 368,328.00 out of the pooled centre APPLH_INFOTECH into PCTECHKCM, and document 5120146901 charges the Saviynt MyHR configuration of 15,813.50 out of the people and culture centre APPLHHR into PCTECHMYHR. Both sig centres are fed from people systems, and rule 7 places the feeding centre on the same destination.

rules.match: Column C equals APPLHFIN.
rules.evidence: Cost centre APPLHFIN carries column D value 'FIN,STRAT,AUDIT,TREAS,GOV AFFAIRS & PROC'. The structure carries Finance as both portfolio and platform. Column N and column K across the centre name the corporate finance product estate and no other: planning and consolidation on ONESTREAM, procurement on JAGGAER, accounts payable automation on TUNGSTEN AUTOMATION, treasury market data on BLOOMBERG, REFINITIV, MOODY'S ANALYTICS, LACIMA and FIS INTEGRITY, expense management on SAP CONCUR, tax on CUMULUS TAX SYSTEMS, and the finance system service requests on FENWICK SOFTWARE. Documents 5120273866, 5120273867 and 5120273872 charge finance service requests between this centre and APPLGENERAL, and rule 19 places the receiving legs on the same destination.

rules.match: Column C equals APPLHHR.
rules.evidence: Cost centre APPLHHR carries column D value 'PEOPLE & CULTURE'. The structure carries P&C as both portfolio and platform. Column N and column K across the centre name the people product estate: SAP SUCCESS FACTOR, WORKDAY PEAKON, CORNERSTONE with LINKEDIN LEARNING, SMARTRECRUITERS, KORN FERRY, REWARD GATEWAY, ELMO and SPINIFEX, together with the quarterly HCALRECHG lines. Document 5120146901 charges the Saviynt MyHR configuration of 15,813.50 out of this centre into PCTECHMYHR, which rule 5 places on the same destination.

rules.match: Column C equals APPLFIREFINING.
rules.evidence: Cost centre APPLFIREFINING carries column D value 'F&I REFINING'. The structure states that Fuel Infrastructure is the refinery and manufacturing business portfolio and carries Manufacturing as a platform. Column N and column K across the centre name refinery process products and no other: ASPEN DMC3 and ASPEN ONE ENGINEERING, AVEVA PI, YOKOGAWA, XHQ, THERMO LIMS and SAMPLEMANAGER, PIPENET, STARTPROF, ANSYS and PAS AUTOMATION INTEGRITY. Document 5116578211 charges the Dragos operational technology monitoring of 44,868.29 into this centre out of the pooled centre APPLH_INFOTECH.

rules.match: Column C equals APPLMTOTAL, APPLBRNDCOMS or APPLRCALSTORES, and column N or column K names the point of sale and back office estate: Vynamic, NAMOS, DOMS, FuelPay or Fuel Pay, BO PC, GVR, ICR or Gilbarco.
rules.evidence: These are the products that run the till, the back office and the forecourt controller at a service station site. Document 5118140897 and the reversal 5118530892 apportion one bundle across two cost centres, and in APPLMTOTAL the bundle reads BO PC, DOMS, FUELPAY, NAMOS SUPPORT and VYNAMICS beside OPT (TT) and COMPAC ONLINE FEE on rule 10, KRONOS on rule 13 and DRIVE OFF on rule 15, while the hardware legs of the one document read ACCENTURE RETAIL SUPPORT, STORE FIELD SUPPORT (FUJITSU), OPT (UGO), SCO, WINDCAVE EFT and UNMANNED OVERNIGHT LICENSE FEE. One document is one accounting event, and the event is the service station estate.

rules.match: Column C equals APPLMTOTAL, APPLBRNDCOMS or APPLRCALSTORES, and column N or column K names an outdoor payment terminal supplier or service: COMPAC, TRANSPONDER, TT FUEL, MECKERING, or OPT read as a whole word.
rules.evidence: OPT must be read as a whole word. Read as a substring it also takes lines carrying OPTIMISER and OPTIMISED, which belong to rules 14 and 16, and the capture becomes 73 lines and minus 76,484.59, a swing of 181,093.88. Outdoor payment terminals sit on the forecourt of a retail site. Document 5118140897 carries OPT (TT) and COMPAC ONLINE FEE inside the store estate bundle that rule 9 rests on. Eleven further documents pair the COMPAC ONLINE FEE, COMPACT OPT and FUEL SUPPLY EMT TT OPT LEGACY legs of this centre against hardware legs of the same cost centre and the same text, and both sides of every one of those pairs carry the one destination.

rules.match: Column C equals APPLMTOTAL, APPLBRNDCOMS or APPLRCALSTORES, and column N or column K names an in store device or in store equipment licence: Squizify, KwickSwitch, Cooper Atkins, Smoodi or GM Vending.
rules.evidence: Each line names a site device, a temperature probe, a tablet pack, a beverage machine licence or a planogram update, and several name the individual retail site the device sits at. The charge is verifiable from the site named in column N.

rules.match: Column C equals APPLMTOTAL, APPLBRNDCOMS or APPLRCALSTORES, and column N or column K names a retail endpoint, site network or application control licence: MERAKI, ITCM, WIN10 or AIRLOCK. The ZEPHYR LICENSE 11X line on sheet row 11883 is excluded and held open at O24.
rules.evidence: Derived from three facts inside the line item tabs, each decisive with zero exceptions for the lines reached. First, document 5118140897 and the reversal 5118530892 carry AIRLOCK, ITCM and MERAKI VPN in the one apportioned bundle as BO PC, DOMS, FUELPAY, NAMOS SUPPORT and VYNAMICS, which rule 9 places on Ampol Retail and Store Operations, and the hardware legs of the one document read ACCENTURE RETAIL SUPPORT, STORE FIELD SUPPORT (FUJITSU) and OPT (UGO). Second, column N names retail outright on the two anchors, 'FUJ- CISCO RENEWAL FOR RETAIL MERAKI VPN' at 20,801.43 and 'IT RETAIL WIN10 ESU 25/26' at 106,024.20 with the matching prepaid transfer. Third, 38 of the 82 lines pair against legs of identical column N text in cost centre APPLB2B in the one document, which is the centre apportionment and not a product split. The remaining lines are accruals and prepaid transfers carrying the same four product texts in column N. The ZEPHYR LICENSE 11X line that an earlier draft carried here rested on a counterpart leg alone and is held open at O24.

rules.match: Column C equals APPLMTOTAL, APPLBRNDCOMS or APPLRCALSTORES, and column N or column K names a retail workforce or facilities platform: Kronos, UKG, LaborPro, Techniche, Ampol FM or AmpolFM.
rules.evidence: These platforms run site labour scheduling and site facilities maintenance for the retail network. The LaborPro lines are 695 near identical per site subscription amounts on one purchase order, 7000251407, from vendor CONNORS AND ASSOCIATES LLC. The twelve monthly AmpolFM allocation lines are negative because the licence is allocated out to another centre in the same document; the opposite legs sit outside this block and stay visible there.

rules.match: Column C equals APPLMTOTAL, APPLBRNDCOMS or APPLRCALSTORES, and column N or column K names the retail fuel pricing platform: PDI, TouchStar or the phase 2 go live of that implementation.
rules.evidence: PDI, supplied by TOUCHSTAR APAC PTY LTD, is the platform that applies fuel prices at the site. The lines are the licence, the phase 2 implementation stages and the externally optimised price module. This is the execution system at the site, distinct from the pricing analytics captured by rule 16.

rules.match: Column C equals APPLMTOTAL, APPLBRNDCOMS or APPLRCALSTORES, and column N or column K names retail loss prevention or in store safety: Scancam, drive off, CCTV, loss prevention or food safety.
rules.evidence: Drive off detection, site closed circuit television, loss prevention upgrades and the food safety program all run inside the retail sites. Scancam Operations is the drive off detection supplier named in column K.

rules.match: Column C equals APPLMTOTAL, APPLBRNDCOMS or APPLRCALSTORES, and column N or column K names a retail data or analytics platform: SNOWFLAKE, SNOWMKT, POWERBI, POWER BI, FABRIC, PRICING OPTIMISER, AZURE CONSUMPTION PRICING, vendor INSURGE PARTNERS, or the SAS licence in either spelling the export carries, 'SAS LICENSING' (9 lines, 498,750.03) and 'SAS LICENCING' (7 lines, minus 0.02).
rules.evidence: The centre match is the first condition and every one of the 69 lines sits in APPLMTOTAL. These lines are the retail share of the data estate: the monthly Snowflake recharges for point of sale and pricing data, the Power BI Fabric retail capacity, the SAS licensing amortisation and the pricing optimiser build and its cloud consumption. The structure carries Retail Data AU as a platform under Ampol Retail. This follows the adjudicated convention that the cost centre in column C decides the destination everywhere except the pooled corporate centre APPLH_INFOTECH, and it follows the mapping values present in the source file, where all 14 Snowflake lines in cost centre APPLCCO read Commercial Fuels and Supply rather than the data portfolio. One line, S12177 on document 5118145663, is the negative leg of a Snowflake reclassification whose positive leg sits on the hardware tab; each leg follows the centre that holds it and the pair is listed in the contra documents.

rules.match: Column C equals APPLMTOTAL, APPLBRNDCOMS or APPLRCALSTORES, and column N contains one of the four source spellings exactly as the export carries the spellings: 'ADOBE CAMPAIGN' (6 lines, 191,392.02), 'D365 CUST' (13 lines, 186,790.32, covering D365 CUST INSIGHTS, D365 CUSTOMER INSIGHTS and D365 CUST SVC), 'CAMPAIGNMONITOR' as one word with no space (14 lines, 832.00) and 'PAGEPROOF' (1 line, 16,480.69).
rules.evidence: The four spellings are quoted from column N, not from the product names, so a reviewer searching the stated text finds the lines: 'CAMPAIGN MONITOR' as two words returns nothing in either tab, and the customer data lines split between D365 CUST INSIGHTS and D365 CUSTOMER INSIGHTS, which the stem 'D365 CUST' covers. Adobe Campaign and Dynamics 365 Customer Insights are the campaign execution and customer data products, CampaignMonitor is the campaign email product and PageProof is the campaign artwork approval product. The structure carries Ampol Loyalty & Martech as a platform under Ampol Customer.

rules.match: Column C equals APPLMTOTAL, APPLBRNDCOMS or APPLRCALSTORES, and column N or column K names a digital channel content or hosting product: Contentstack, Sitecore, web hosting, CSC Corporate Domains, domain management, MozSEO, Google Map or vendor LIVELI PTY LTD.
rules.evidence: These are the content management, web hosting, domain and site search products behind the public digital channel, all in cost centre APPLBRNDCOMS. Six documents pair the WEB HOSTING AZURE CONSUMPTION legs of this centre, 59,157.25, against equal and opposite legs in the pooled centre APPLH_INFOTECH, so the hosting of the public channel is charged out of the pool and lands on the centre that carries the channel.

rules.evidence: HighRadius is the receivables product behind the invoice to cash project, on purchase orders 7000248759, 7000248770 and 7000248998. notes: Every one of the 3,551 lines maps through exactly one numbered rule or one open item. No line is captured twice: the rule matches were tested against every line and produced no collision.

Mapping values present in the source file, column A and column B, are absent from all seventeen cost centres in this block, so no rule here can contradict a mapping value. Those values were still used as the pattern: in the centres that carry those rows, individual licence lines follow the cost centre to the business portfolio rather than to a product owner, and a data platform recharge stays on the business centre. Rules 6, 7, 8 and 16 follow that pattern.

The marketing group, cost centres APPLMTOTAL, APPLBRNDCOMS and APPLRCALSTORES, carries no single centre destination. It splits on the row through rules 9 to 18, which is why an individual licence line inside those centres is held open at O3 rather than placed.

The security lines in this block stay with the holding cost centre, and the adjudication upheld that reading. The convention settled is that the cost centre in column C decides the destination everywhere except the pooled corporate centre APPLH_INFOTECH, and that naming a security product does not by itself place a line on Cyber. The decisive proof is a dollar identity on Dragos: the invoice in APPLH_INFOTECH is 164,595.77, document 5116578210 recharges 52,627.47 and 44,868.29 out, and the residual of 67,100.01 is the amount phaseb_b2 rule 52 carries on Cyber. The 44,868.29 receiving leg is the 'DRAGOS OT MONITORING' line in cost centre APPLFIREFINING and stays on rule 8, and the three CyberCX Saviynt configuration lines in APPLHHR at 44,810.25 gross stay on rule 7 for the same reason.

Cost centre APPLGENERAL, column D value 'NON FUNCTIONAL AREAS', carries no single destination and is split on the row: rules 19 and 20 place the receivables and planning products on Finance, and the remainder sits at open items O17, O18, O19 and O20.
Destinations are taken only from the portfolio and platform table in the structure document, spelled as that table spells each one. No other source places a line in this block.
